text:
Buffalo is a .500 team by the chances and a slightly worse one by the scoreboard, and the gap is shooting. The Sabres have taken exactly 50% of the expected goals this season but scored about six fewer goals than those chances usually bring. At 8-6-3 and 19 points, our simulations give them a 36% playoff chance, with a projection near 90 points.

The good news is where the play is coming from. Jack Quinn, Noah Ostlund and Zach Benson have been one of the better lines we track: 66% of the expected goals together and an 8-2 edge in goals over 118 minutes. Tage Thompson, after a position change that had Buffalo Hockey Beat writing about him eyeing 50 goals, has also been productive with Peyton Krebs and Benson (7-1 in goals). Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen has been better than his save rate looks, 3.7 goals saved above expected over his last five starts.

The frustrating part is nights like Sunday: 78 shot attempts to 51 against Vegas, a 4-1 loss, and Adin Hill in the way. When a team keeps outplaying people and losing anyway, the results usually turn. Usually. The Sabres' week ahead will tell you whether this is a slow start or a pattern, and the line to watch is Quinn's, because when it's on the ice Buffalo looks like a playoff team.
